title: Behold, I Am Coming Soon
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Jesus is coming again, not quietly but with his reward in hand. His delay is mercy, and only those washed in the blood of the Lamb will stand.
exhortation: Jesus is coming soon. And he comes again not as he first arrived, in the quiet of a manger, but with his recompense in hand. Every soul will one day stand before his judgment seat. That should drive us to ask: is it today? Is it tomorrow? We don't know the hour, but the shadows of this earth are surely lengthening, and the day is coming.

We can't mistake the Lord's patience for indifference. He doesn't count slowness as we do. His delay is the door of mercy staying open a little longer. But he is also the Alpha and the Omega. In Colossians Paul writes that Christ is the firstborn of all creation. By his hand the universe was made, by his word it is upheld, and by his will it holds together. He who stood at the beginning will stand at the end.

When he returns in judgment, only one company of people will be able to stand: those washed white in the blood of the Lamb. So let none of us be deceived by fair speech or hollow doctrine. Don't take comfort in any religion that promises you heaven while letting your heart remain a playground for sin. To claim salvation while walking in sexual immorality, harboring idols and nursing hatred in your heart is to embrace a delusion. You cannot love the darkness and claim to know the light. God will not be mocked.

The testimony of God is sure. His angel delivered this truth to the churches once for all, so that no one has an excuse. Christ is the root and the descendant of David. He is coming. He is the bright morning star, and when he appears, his brilliance will be so great that he will be our light. The sun and moon will have fulfilled their purpose. So let's remember Jesus this morning: he is coming soon, he is risen, and he is reigning.
prayer: What a day that will be, Lord, and what a hope we have. You are the beginning and the end, the first and the last. You came and died and bore our sin, and you will come again and vanquish all sin and every enemy. Death will be defeated, and we will see it with our own eyes. What a joy that will be.

Help us live this day in light of that day, so that we don't forget. Open our eyes to see a harvest of souls who need to hear the gospel, and help us live in obedience to you, in a way that honors and glorifies your name, until the day you come. In Jesus' name.
